extra.message: The 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system(). An attacker with the internal ops token can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. host='127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection; an attacker can supply expressions like '{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__("os").popen("id").read() }}' to achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The client-supplied JSON body ('filter' key, or the whole payload) is passed unvalidated as the MongoDB query filter to find_one(). An attacker can inject query operators (e.g. {"$where": ...} or {"$ne": null}) to bypass intended filtering or extract unauthorized data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: The 'packet_ref' request parameter is joined directly into a filesystem path with no sanitization of path separators or '..' segments, then written with arbitrary request body bytes. A value like '../../../../etc/cron.d/evil' allows writing files outside the intended incoming directory.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The 'name' request parameter is joined directly into a filesystem path with no sanitization, then the request body is written to it. A value containing '../' segments allows writing arbitrary files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: Unlike every other handler in this router, ticket_queue_fold_060 has no gate_ref=Depends(_wrk_gate) dependency and no other authentication check, yet returns an 'ops_memo' string explicitly containing 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details'. Any unauthenticated caller can retrieve this sensitive operational data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Authorization for elevated access ('payroll': 'full', 'casework': 'open') is decided purely by comparing a client-supplied cookie ('ops_badge') or header ('x-ops-badge') to the literal string 'lead'. Any caller can set this cookie/header themselves to escalate privileges, since it is never validated against a trusted session or server-side role.

The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is dynamically set to reflect the caller-supplied Origin header, while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This lets any origin make credentialed cross-origin requests (cookies/session included), defeating the same-origin policy and enabling cross-site data theft or CSRF-like attacks against authenticated sessions.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The 'lane' query parameter is passed unvalidated to RedirectResponse. An attacker can craft a link to this endpoint with lane set to an external URL to redirect victims to an attacker-controlled site (e.g. for phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The full client-supplied JSON payload is merged into a privileged object (workset.update(payload)) that includes 'approved' and 'balance' fields, with no allow-list of permitted keys or validation. A caller can set approved=true or an arbitrary balance directly, bypassing any intended business logic that should govern these fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The raw request body and the full Authorization header (bearer token) are written to the application log at WARNING level. Anyone with log access can capture valid bearer credentials, enabling session/account takeover.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The 'count' query parameter has no upper bound and is used directly to size an in-memory list comprehension (range(count)). A caller can pass an extremely large count (e.g. 10**9) to exhaust server memory/CPU and cause a denial of service.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The 'nonce'/'code' value is generated with the non-cryptographic random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) rather than the secrets module. If this code is used for any security purpose (nonce, token, one-time code) its output is predictable, since Python's random module is not suitable for security-sensitive values.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG

extra.message: The session cookie is set with secure=False, meaning the browser will transmit the authentication token over plain HTTP as well as HTTPS. If any part of the deployment is reachable over HTTP or via a network attacker, the session token can be intercepted and used to hijack the account.

The handler explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' (disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter) and an empty Content-Security-Policy header (removing any script-source restriction). Both weaken the client-side defenses against injected script content.

An internal exception message that embeds the server's private filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) is returned directly in the JSON error response body, disclosing internal deployment details to the caller.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The endpoint returns the raw APP_ENV environment variable and the server's internal export directory path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in the response body, exposing deployment/configuration details useful for further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: MD5 is used to compute a digest of user-supplied input. MD5 is cryptographically broken (collision-prone) and unsuitable if this digest is ever relied on for integrity or security verification rather than a non-security checksum.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The internal ops token check compares the client-supplied header value to the expected secret using the standard '!=' operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. This timing difference can theoretically be used to brute-force the token byte-by-byte instead of using a constant-time comparison (e.g. secrets.compare_digest).

Default values for database_url (embedding the credentials 'supportdesk:supportdesk') and session_secret ('dev-session-secret-change-me') are hardcoded directly in source. If these Settings defaults are ever relied on outside local development (env vars not overridden), a well-known password and secret are used in production.
